decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY captures the Hero V height study but omits the rule that percentage increases are calculated relative to each individual V's total height.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Somewhere my intended message got lost in translation. I know it’s hard to read my mind when I use more abstract terms, and I think I was trying to ask you to change too many things at once, which is why we have taken a couple of steps in the wrong direction.

I’m attaching this image for reference because it was the closest rendering to what I wanted to refine. Instead of changing the length and exploring the terminations at the same time, we’re going to focus strictly on height.

Could you please show the following as a calibrated progression in both the Hero V and the second V? The second V should remain proportionally scaled to its own size, so each increase should be calculated relative to the total height of that individual V.

Original Option B as the control
Original Option B with the right endpoint approximately 1% higher
The same treatment at approximately 2% higher
The same treatment at approximately 3% higher

Please keep the existing slope, terminal shape, taper, and all other geometry exactly as shown in the original Option B. Only the height of the right endpoint should change. Once the correct percentage is established, the É accent should follow that same proportional relationship.

I know this is an exceptionally small distinction, but I believe the relationship between the left and right endpoints will become one of the defining details shared across the Hero V, second V, and É accent. I want it to be almost imperceptible, but still enough to distinguish it from a more average V.

Thank you for helping me isolate it with this level of precision.

value_updates.endpoint_height_scaling_rule: Calculate each percentage increase relative to the total height of the individual V

decisions.reason: The proportional endpoint-height study preserves the second V's subordinate visual role and existing hierarchy; it changes glyph geometry rather than the hierarchy rule.
The source changes only the endpoint-height study for the V-system glyphs and does not alter the E or L letterform requirements.
Only the right endpoint height changes; the second V's left arm and the E/L cap-height alignment reference remain unchanged.
The source concerns glyph endpoint geometry and does not change the selected champagne finish or material distribution.
The source preserves the existing peak-alignment requirement by directing the accent to follow the selected proportional relationship; it does not replace or modify the alignment rule.
The endpoint-height study leaves the selected Balanced Flow kerning and wordmark spacing unchanged.
Changing only the right endpoint height does not alter the common baseline defined by the bottom points of the two Vs and the E/L baseline.
The source supplies design direction but does not change the standing requirement to explain the rationale behind review rounds.
The source does not discuss attachment format, file compatibility, or proof delivery.
